description: Bounds of the line structure preserving split. On a page whose declared policy raises one of 'policy_flags', a paragraph that was assembled from records -- a contents entry of title, leader, folio and byline, one entry to a line -- is cut back into the source lines it was assembled from, so that a record reaches the translator as one unit rather than as a stream. The line carrier the paragraph finder built is gone by the time this runs: 'StylesAndFormulas.process_page_styles' rebuilds every paragraph as style runs, and a style run crosses line boundaries, so lines are recovered from the geometry the characters still carry. The recovery is the paragraph finder's own threading scan, run over characters rather than compositions: the paragraph's vertical range is scanned at 'scan_step' and a position crossed by fewer than 'min_gap_collisions' characters is a gap between lines. 'flat_paragraph_height' is the vertical span below which a paragraph cannot hold two lines and is left whole, which is also the guard that keeps the scan off a degenerate range. 'min_line_characters' is how many non-space characters a recovered line must carry to be a record of its own; below it the line stays with the line above, which keeps a stray mark from becoming a paragraph. A declared page is not all records, though: a contents page can carry an editorial column beside the entries, and cutting running prose into lines would hand the translator a unit that is half a sentence. So two bounds narrow what may be cut, and both have to hold. 'max_line_chars' is the largest a paragraph's mean line may be, counted in non-space characters per recovered line: a record line is short because the record is short, and a line of a prose column is as long as the measure allows. 'require_style_heterogeneity' asks that the paragraph's lines are not all set in the same faces -- a record whose byline or leader is set in another face says so at the line boundary, while a prose column is one face throughout. It is written as 0 or 1 because the bounded configuration reader takes numbers and vocabularies; the faces of a line are its font ids, and a size difference inside one face is not read as a boundary, which keeps the test on the conservative side. Both bounds were calibrated two-sided on a page carrying both shapes at once, and the margins are recorded in the batch report. 'sidecar_fields' and 'exemption_fields' are the format of one split and one exemption record, asserted against the records the pass builds, and 'exemption_reasons' is the closed set of reasons an exemption may name, so the report's shape is declared here rather than implied by the code. A record is not always one line, and which it is on a page is read off the page rather than declared for it. Inside one paragraph the vertical distances between consecutive lines are measured and their median taken, and a distance of at least 'record_gap_ratio' of that median is a record boundary: records are set apart from each other and the lines inside one record are set close, which is the printer's own mechanism rather than a description of any particular page. A paragraph in which no distance reaches the bound has one peak and no boundary to find, and there the line is the record, which is what this pass has always done. A paragraph in which some distance does reach it is cut into the groups the distances mark instead, each group one paragraph placed in its own band, and the lines inside a group are not cut apart, because a record spread over three tight lines is one entry and one translation unit. Every paragraph this pass builds is given the style its own characters are mostly set in rather than the style of the paragraph it came out of: the base style is what the translation is laid out in, and a title line and the byline under it inheriting one style is how a title comes to be printed at byline size. 'policy_flags' is the closed set of policy keys whose truth declares a page, and it is the only place a page type reaches this pass: the code reads the flag, never a type name.
